chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who appointed a man to handle his wife's affairs and ordered him to divorce her according to the Sunnah, and he divorced her three times in one sitting, he said: 'She is returned to the Sunnah (i.e., the third divorce is not final/expulsive), so when three months or three menstrual periods have passed, she has become permanently divorced by one (divorce).'

key_terms.بَانَتْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ: She has become permanently divorced by one
key_terms.تُرَدُّ إِلَى السُّنَّةِ: She is returned to the Sunnah (status of revocability)
key_terms.عَلَى السُّنَّةِ: According to the Sunnah (referring to a single, revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a delegated divorcee pronounces three divorces in one sitting?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the mechanism of 'Taliq al-Talaq' (delegated divorce), establishing that when a delegate pronounces three divorces in one sitting, they are treated as a single revocable divorce rather than three immediate final ones. The wife remains in the 'Sunnah' state until the completion of three months or three menstrual cycles, after which the divorce becomes final and permanent. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the distinction between immediate finality and the waiting period (Iddah) in determining the status of the marriage.
